Pots for flowers have always been something I’ve found surprisingly difficult to make work. Perhaps some of that comes from pigeon-holing myself stylistically into a world of vessels that don’t always feel particularly welcoming, but I have tried to find forms that work. I’ve always preferred bud vases, forms with narrow openings designed for just a couple of stems, rather than larger vessels intended for bouquets and sprawling arrangements. I think that’s why I’ve ended up making quite simple cylindrical vases for lone stems and foliage, or forms where the rim slopes gradually inwards towards a narrow opening. For the most part, they’re essentially the same shape as the cylinder, just taking a different journey towards the opening. But I don’t think I’ve been entirely fair to flower pots. Perhaps some of it is simply my own lack of ability when it comes to arranging flowers and branches in my pots. Truthfully, it’s never really been something I’ve sought to do. When I first started making pottery, I was much more interested in making things to eat and drink from than I was in making things for displaying flowers. But I’d like to change that. My mum always has pots filled with flowers at home, and on the rare occasions I’ve brought some greenery into the studio, it’s always felt like a breath of fresh air. My workshop very rarely feels like a place where I can actually see and use pots for their intended purpose, and perhaps that’s where some of the problem lies. So, here’s a vase that I’m partly happy with, made for, and actually used for, its intended purpose. I like the shape, although I’m less keen on the glaze. I’ll have to make some more. #flowervase #vase #pottery #ceramics #clay

In this Tips video I go over how I cut my pieces off of the hump. I’ve seen quite a few different techniques from various potters on this process, but I’ve found this to be what works for me. I can’t stress enough practicing the technique before committing to trying to make pots to alleviate a lot of the frustration that can come from figuring it out. I think a lot of people give up on it because of this and as we all know, persistence pays off in ceramics. I hope this video helps and I’ll keep making them…If anybody’s interested in learning more about these techniques I do have a workshop coming up in January at Jewell Town Pottery in Massachusetts. Feel free to give them a shout and inquire about availability.                                          #potterytips #learning #ceramics #pottery #wheelthrown
